requirements.statement: Each passage of text that constitutes a heading is structured as a heading with one of the accepted markups.

citations.quote: chaque passage de texte constituant un titre est-il structuré à l’aide d’une balise `<hx>` ou d’une balise possédant un attribut WAI-ARIA `role="heading"` associé à un attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-level` ?
Si c’est le cas pour chaque titre, **le test est validé**.

routes.statement: The heading is an <hx> element, x being a number from 1 to 6.

citations.quote: Soit il est structuré au moyen d’une balise `<hx>` (“x” désignant une valeur numérique comprise entre 1 et 6);

routes.statement: The heading is an element with role="heading" and an aria-level attribute whose value is a number.

citations.quote: Soit il est structuré au moyen d’une balise possédant un attribut WAI-ARIA `role="heading"` et un attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-level=x` (“x” désignant une valeur numérique).
WAI-ARIA permet de définir des titres via le rôle `heading` et l’attribut `aria-level` (indication du niveau de titre).

rationale.text:
The test applies to each passage of text that constitutes a heading, and finding those passages is judgment: the methodology starts from the headings identified in test 9.1.1, and whether a bold line, a large paragraph or a styled div is a heading depends on what it means on the page. Two routes are accepted: an element, or an element with role="heading" and a numeric aria-level. No check can say which texts are headings, so no fault proves the test fails and no clean result proves it passes. The candidate is none. axe's p-as-heading is tagged and linked as evidence only, although axe marks it experimental and off by default: it is the only tool-side hint that a paragraph styled like a heading lacks heading markup. It looks only at

elements, skips any element whose role is already heading, and guesses from weight, size and italics compared with the following paragraphs, so its fault does not prove the paragraph is a heading and its clean result says nothing about other elements. It examines whether a

uses either markup, so it names both routes, with scope partial. A custom check is linked the same way: it lists elements with a role="heading" token that are not and have no aria-level, or one whose value is not a positive integer. The author marked such an element as a heading, but it meets neither route as the methodology words them. Whether the element really is a passage of text constituting a heading is still judgment, for example a role put on a large container by mistake, so its fault is evidence only and its scope partial. Applicability is judgment: whether any text on the page constitutes a heading cannot be decided by code. Needs is empty.
